findings.what: "so it can only raise the real current a little above the readout" puts an unsourced size on the hull's effect, and it is likely wrong: the hull path between two bonded frames can carry most of the return and raise the current well above the cable-loop figure, so drop "a little".

findings.where: Screen 5 (and any live drop), readouts and breaker bars
findings.what: While the loop lights, the current tile and bars count up (113 A, 332 A, 532 A) beside 440 V and 0.8 Ω, and the breaker labels read "No instant trip" before flipping, so mid-motion the screen shows sums that break I = V ÷ Z and hints that the fault current builds over a second; show the settled current as the loop lights.

"The readouts show 0 V and 0 A" is false once he moves the live phase picker (the moved state shows L2, 440 V and 169 A under that sentence), so tie it to L1: "With L1 chosen, the readouts show 0 V and 0 A."
The tile reads 0.8 Ω while the words say no loop is driven, and screen 1's tile says "No loop", which leaves it unclear whether there is a loop; say the loop exists but nothing drives it.
The key claim, that L2 and L3 now sit 440 V from the hull, is told but never drawn; a "Hull at L1" or "440 V to hull" mark would let the picture show why a same-phase second fault drives nothing.

The read keeps only the numbers and drops the screen's point (the short lasts until a slower trip acts, heats the cables, and the pair with the highest loops is the one to check), so the read-through and the Book lose it.
The read runs to 24 words and drops "a short between phases, through the hull", the lesson's headline; split it and keep that phrase.
The opener "Still there." is cryptic; say what it means or cut it.
"When the circuits match, that is double one circuit's." ends on a dangling possessive; say "double one circuit's loop impedance".
"Check that pair." reads like an instruction to do something on the screen; say "A design check uses that pair."
"One insulation failure on either joins them to L1" should be "joins it to L1", since one failure joins one phase.
A recall question about an earthed supply sits over the insulated board, and the right Check labels Z1 on the insulated feeder, which blurs which system the 635 A belongs to.

The second half ("The leads limit the short across the bench. Both circuits' cable loops limit...") states a likeness, not a break; state the difference: thick leads let the battery short run huge, while a ship's cable loops can hold a second fault below an instant trip.
"the bench shorts the battery, through both leads" is unclear with three leads on the bench; name the red and black leads.
"Counting the cable loops alone gives the smaller, safer current" reads as if a smaller current were safer; say that counting only the cable loops errs on the safe side for the trip check.
"A second fault on a different phase does" (trip) is stated flat, but the lesson then shows a 314 A pair that does not trip instantly; say "is meant to".

"That compares three-wire supplies with the same line voltage" is confusing, because the earthed side's earth fault is driven line to earth; say "an insulated board with no neutral against an earthed board of the same line voltage".
"Until it is cleared, ..." (23 words) and the rule of thumb (22 words) run past 20 words; split each.

The brief promised a pointer to BS 7671 Regulation 411.6.4 by number and a "time with the first fault" card showing the healthy phases' insulation at 173%, and neither appears; one practice line naming 411.6.4 as the rule to look up would serve him as an electrician.
The two boxes on the feeders are the breakers but carry no label, while "Breaker 1" and "Breaker 2" sit beside the current bars at the edges, so the link between box and bar is left to guess.
The loop's glow running down the supply card's right edge touches the "y" of "Supply".
In dark mode the second-fault loop's pink is close to L3's magenta, so a loop on L3 is harder to pick out from the conductor.
The lesson column sits in the left half of the card and leaves the right half empty.
Its title is the web host "cdn.standards.iteh.ai" instead of the standard's name, IEC 60364-4-41.
